Review: This is proof that you don't need a silver fork to eat good food. An Italian restaurant that makes authentic Italian food accessible and affordable! An Italian restaurant that makes authentic Italian food accessible and affordable! The ingredients are high-quality, they serve REAL Italian herb sausages, and the marinara tomato sauce is not cheap prego tomato ketchup! I recommend this place to anyone for an introduction to proper, real Italian food. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion. The place is no-frills and cosy and the service was very polite, friendly and warm. No shortcuts, no Malaysian-ised (cili sauce, mayo, frozen vege, cheap processed ingredients substitutions).The menu that has a huge selection of oven-baked pizzas, platters, pastas, starters, appetisers, salads and desserts. Many of the items can only be found in fancy restaurants. The huge oven can be seen at the entrance!What I had: Starter: a delicious and crispy fried cheese ravioli with marinara dipping sauce. Main: Hot platter sausage parmesan with toasted garlic baguette and a bowl of pasta of my choice - Served in really generous portion, perfect for big eaters or sharing so the tummy can try other items. Highly recommended! Dessert : Spumoni, an Italian gelato ice cream of 3 layers, cherry, vanilla and pistachio. Tart, creamy and refreshing! What a unique taste!I will definitely come again to be transported in Italy!Advisable you order to take away if you're ordering for a big family.
Location: 169, Jalan Rawa, Taman Amira, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: Avijit Das Patnaik - The 'Pattu'
Review: This has to be the best genuine Indian paratha place in south east asia. Being a food blogger and explore myself can vouch with some authority. The real authentic Punjabi style paratha with thick fillings. And that dollop of butter. We …MoreThis has to be the best genuine Indian paratha place in south east asia. Being a food blogger and explore myself can vouch with some authority. The real authentic Punjabi style paratha with thick fillings. And that dollop of butter. We visited this place for three consecutive days! Aloo paratha, Paneer Paratha are excellent and Gobi paratha with the crunchy bites of cauliflower pieces even better. Sarson da saag is another must try dish here. The kalakund, cham cham and few other sweets also good. Service is fast and staff are very humble and gentle people. For a Johor Bahru food trail this place is a must to visit and it’s barely 750m away from the immigration CIQ checkpoint. The Budget? Well barely 30MYR = 10SGD = 8USD for four parathas, couple of sweets and two plates of sarson da saag.. enough to feed 3-4 pax!!If you love to travel on a budget and seek value for money then my book on Amazon & Kindle should help you. Do search for ‘Scissors Paper Stones - A Family Budget travel guide’ in Amazon or kindle or Goodreads, to buy. Travel more to save more!
Location: 418-5, 418-5, Jalan Trus, Bandar Johor Bahru, Johor Bahru, Johor

Review: I went to Chez Papa French to celebrate my boyfriend birthday, I got a shock that it require a smart casual attire (no slippers, no singlets, no shorts), but thankfully the owner was really nice to let us in still and provide us with crocs. …MoreI went to Chez Papa French to celebrate my boyfriend birthday, I got a shock that it require a smart casual attire (no slippers, no singlets, no shorts), but thankfully the owner was really nice to let us in still and provide us with crocs. They provide free bread before the meal which I thought was really nice. For appetisers we had French Onion Soup which I thought was really nice, big portion with a huge slab of cheese on top, herbs and caramelised onions. We also had scallops and prawns with a white wine cream sauce which was I find the the cream sauce was special because they added white wine, for this the portion is really small 2 scallops and 2 prawns, but it was just nice for us because only 2 of us. For mains (forgot to take picture) we had sirloin steak, medium rare as what we wanted and the pepper cream sauce is also nice. We also ordered a pesto linguine, which was really nice as well, though I find it a little too creamy, and the portion was huge so at the end it felt too jelak. I also like their service, because it was my boyfriend birthday they gave complimentary cake with ice cream and drew out the words Happy Birthday and even sang the birthday song. They really go the extra miles for their customers and deserve 5 star, because you know they don’t have to but they choose to. Overall really a pleasant place for special occasion and would definitely come back and try their other dishes.
Restaurant: Chez Papa French Bistro and Wine Bar

Author: Aloysius Kwok
Review: Went there for dinner at about 8pm. There were a total of 3 groups of customers, including ourselves, in the restaurant. However, it was just left with us after 9pm. My fianceé was offered a free hair band before we ordered our food. …MoreWent there for dinner at about 8pm. There were a total of 3 groups of customers, including ourselves, in the restaurant. However, it was just left with us after 9pm. My fianceé was offered a free hair band before we ordered our food.The kitchen staff seemed a lot more attentive than the waiter and waitress. When they noticed that our fire was out, they asked if we wanted them to light up the fire again. And when I dropped by chopsticks on the floor, the kitchen staff who was resting at the table across us offered a new pair of chopsticks.The concept is similar to hotpot. However, you cannot just choose a soup base. You have to order the fish, or the seafood platter. Then you can choose your soup, and subsequently add on any additional ingredients, such as meat, seafood, vegetables or staples to cook in the pot.We chose the mushroom seafood soup, which came with generous portions of enoki mushrooms, some king oyster mushrooms, sliced potatoes and cabbage. I was not able taste any seafood, and I thought it tasted more like just mushroom soup.The handmade noodles looked like mee pok, but tasted slightly better than mee pok. However, I personally do not like to have my mee pok with soup.I paid a total of 107.60MYR for 2 persons. We only ordered the seabass, mud crab, abalone, and handmade noodles.I thought that the overall taste was so-so, nothing special. The only thing I liked was the attentive staffs. However, I cannot comment much on the food because we did not order much food. Perhaps adding other ingredients into the soup might have made my experience more impressionable. However, I did not think that it was worth paying so much money for the ingredients in Malaysia.

Review: The entrance leads to a dim and relaxing interior that exudes rustic charm, with chilling jazz playing up the mood.  The servers,  pleasant and polite, showed us to our table. …MoreThe entrance leads to a dim and relaxing interior that exudes rustic charm, with chilling jazz playing up the mood.  The servers,  pleasant and polite, showed us to our table.Seafood platter in Spicy Sichuan Mala soup base.  I chose the ‘Medium’ level of spiciness, just to be safe.   Scallops, crabs, prawns, squids, mussels, bamboo shellfish and Lala bathing in and soaking up all the goodness and flavors of the ‘Sichuan Mala’ broth.  This invoked memories of my work and holidays in Tianjin, Beijing, Shenzhen and Sichuan.A small flame alight below the platter keep them warm and bubbling away happily in their sumptuous jacuzzi.  Handmade noodles goes well with the broth.  Dip some fried buns into the savoury aromatic Mala broth.  Divine!Sipping Korean Soju together and exchanging kind words reignite sweet memories from more than one or even two decades of friendship.A big fat Red Snapper arrived shortly.  It was soaking up all the goodness in a platter with ‘Seafood Mushroom’ broth bubbling slowly, over a small flame.  We tore into big fat fish and scooped a generous portion to eat.  So tender and juicy, it was bursting with flavours we can’t stop.As we kept the Soju ambrosia flowing, we reminisced happily and randomly munch on crunchy fish skins and chips.  We totally enjoyed the excellent food and rustic ambience in the wonderful company of close friends.Fat Fish JB seafood restaurant is an excellent choice, for celebration and gathering with family and friends.
Location: 97, Jln Beringin, Taman Melodies, Johor Bahru, Johor

Never went there before so I couldn't compare it with previous experience, but I definitely won't miss going back.

Author: Lucretia Mazzeschi
Review: DISGRACE TO MY COUNTRYWell... …MoreDISGRACE TO MY COUNTRYWell...I arrived at this restaurant very hungry and very excited to try the much praised food of all the reviews I had previously seen.It was about 6 pm when I arrived, me and my boyfriend ordered the following dishes- ravioli ( he had pesto sauce and I had tomato sauce)- milanese- pizza with arugula and hamWhen the ravioli came I knew exactly what to expect, these did not look at all like the “home made “ ravioli described in the reviews, the sauce tasted so artificial that I wouldn’t be surprised if it was PREGO sauce.I sent all my ravioli back without even touching them, and when the waiter asked if there was something wrong with the dish I clearest said that it was no good,The Milanese was an offense to my country!We had just came back from a two month vacation in Italy, eating plenty of authentic Milanese, this didn’t even look like one.For the ones that might not know Milanese is a THIN piece of meat ( usually lamb, pork or chicken) that has been FLATTENED, COATED IN BREADCRUMBS AND PARMESAN and FRIED IN BUTTER!!!!!! The one presented in front of us at this restaurant wasn’t even coated in anything, was simply a pork chop! ( don’t write Milanese if you don’t know what it is)The pizza was dough was not left to raise long enough, was acidic, not digestible and undercooked.Had one slice and left it for the kitchen to enjoy!The ham on top was not ham, maybe American style ham...Anyways we left unsatisfied, hungry and with a bill of 260  rm for some terrible food.I don’t blame by any means the waiters of the kitchen staff that was not italian and could have not knows, but the owner that is a disgrace to my country!If you are going to call your restaurant Coppola’s Family style Italian restaurant or whatever make sure that. What you serve is up to the standards not something I could find better at the premade section of a supermarket!And this is for the owner :Se apre un ristorante all’estero e crede di essere furbo solo perché le persone del posto non conoscono il vero sapore del cibo si sbaglia di grosso! Forse il 90% penserà che il suo cibo sia buono machi se ne intende sa benesimo che il suo cibo è un’offesa all’italia ed ai cittadini italiani.Con questo concludo la mia recensione e vado a postarl su altri social media, perché la gente deve sapere cosa si mette in bocca!

Author: Khamael Chong
Review: Had the TWG high tea set for two. Rm68 inclusive of taxes. In all we had 11 item in the set:1. Pandan chicken …MoreHad the TWG high tea set for two. Rm68 inclusive of taxes. In all we had 11 item in the set:1. Pandan chicken2. Lemongrass prawn ball3. Macaron4. Smoked salmon open face finger sandwich5. Mini croissant with Thai basil minced chicken filling6. Som tam salad served in shotglass7. Red ruby with jackfruit in coconut milk8. Scones with jam and cream9. Egg tarts10. Thai mango with glutinuous rice11. Brownie with vanilla  ice cream and chocolate sauceThe set came with a mug of TWG tea, ours was Moroccan mint.Overall the taste of most items were pleasant. The most impressive and delicious was probably the brownie, which we requested to serve last. There was quite a show when the waiter poured the warm chocolate sauce on the the brownie, as it sizzled rather excitingly on the hot plate the brownie was served on. The warm and rich texture of the brownie together the bittersweet chocolate sauce and cold vanilla ice cream was an immediate pleasure to the palate, and me and my wife both enjoyed it immensely, and straight after immediately rated in our No.1 amongst all the food items.The croissant was also well made with rich buttery flaky texture, albeit on the cold side since it must have been awhile since it left the oven. The combination of savoury basil chicken with the buttery croissant was also a winning combo.My wife's favourite was the Pandan chicken, which was savoury and slightly sweet with a hit of spices and gentle pandan fragrance. This dish together with the lemongrass prawn could do better if they were served hot immediately off the pan/ grill.The only not so great item was the macarons, which were overly sweet. 'Nuf said.Generally all the flavours were well balanced and the sweet items were surprisingly not sickeningly sweet, which gave us a pleasant surprise (with the exception of Macarons). The tea was also nice and a great palate cleanser with a refreshing mint taste. We polished off everything else and returned home full and satisfied.Definitely worth a return visit.
Location: 82C, Jalan Trus, Bandar Johor Bahru, Johor Bahru, Johor

Overrated.

Review: At a glance, the menu may seem a little limited—maybe even far from offering anything you would be willing to stop by to eat; however, if you can get past your inhibitions and just give it a try, you may be surprised by what you find. …MoreAt a glance, the menu may seem a little limited—maybe even far from offering anything you would be willing to stop by to eat; however, if you can get past your inhibitions and just give it a try, you may be surprised by what you find. Prices are definitely on the high side, probably averaging about RM40–50 per person, depending on what you order.The joint is found in a two-story shophouse, with most of its seating on the second floor. Steps are narrow (and one was slightly shaky), so patrons who are less mobile may want to stick to the ground floor. To some degree, the cafe can cater to patrons with prams—though fitting more than two prams on premise (and on the ground floor only) may not be possible if other patrons and staff are to still be able to get around somewhat comfortably.The recommended Flowers Breakfast somewhat lived up to the hype around it. The meal is definitely filling (and that full feeling will last for quite a while); its scrambled eggs were well done and uniquely flavoured, and the bread used for the toast was excellent. Even the fruit component of the dish went surprisingly well with the other ‘dishes’ it was served with.For a side, I had the Wedges with Tar Tar sauce dip—this one could do with more flavour; the sauce was also a tad runny.Drink-wise, I had their Thyme Lemonade special as well as a taste of their Pineapple Lemonade, and another drink that had pomegranates in it (sorry, I forgot the name of the last drink). I would describe the sensation they all gave as refreshing, though each one had its own unique flavour and oomph. I’m partial towards the thyme lemonade and pomegranate drink.Their cakes appear to all be made in-House, and tend to be displayed in a cake display of sorts, so dry edges are inevitable, though the insides remain nicely moist and buttery (this is based solely on their pistachio cake).Overall an alright place.Would I visit it again? Maybe.

Review: Very impressed with the entire experience. The moment you step in, you feel that grungy rustic atmosphere. …MoreVery impressed with the entire experience. Had a nice time chatting with them about everything under the sun and you can tell they love their jobs.One way for me to see if a restaurant serves good food is how the staff behave. If the food is good, they'll get compliments to pass on to the chefs and they'll feel proud to work there.On that note, the food. Seriously woah. Legit good.The steak was seasoned just right, thick cut and the char smelled so smoky. That's the best part cause all the flavour is there.And here's the thing I was particularly impressed with: The accompanying sides are usually complimentary to the steak because the star is the steak. But their sides were so good that I had such a hard time deciding what to savour and what to move on to!- Pumpkin mash was so light, fluffy and packed with flavour.- Asparagus had peeled skin which showed attention to detail- Grilled cherry tomatoes that also had a smoky char to it- Mushroom with veggies were so savoury and aromatic- Rocket salad was tossed in a tangy sauce accompanied with fresh pops of small red peppercorns- This helped cut the surfeitness ('jelatness')Man... Just wish I had another tummy to go for a 2nd round.It is definitely on the pricier side. Was RM190 for a sirloin and sides so gotta prepare yourself mentally, especially if you're going for the higher cuts.Personally, I try the sirloin at any steakhouse because it is the best benchmark. Properly seared fat cap, yet not too fatty on the meat area which means seasoning must be done right else the steak wouldn't come through in flavour and so forth.If they get the sirloin right, they're worth it. (getting wagyu tasty isn't a benchmark to me cause the meat alone is that good of a quality. To mess it up will be...)But to each his own! They definitely got their sirloin right

Author: Toh Bee Leng
Review: We ordered a plate of Dang Gui Roast Duck, a plate of Shi Quan Roast Duck and a plate of Char Siew Roast Pork . The sauce of the Dang Gui Roast Duck was punched with full flavour. The sauce of the Shi Quan Roast Duck was diluted. The Char …MoreWe ordered a plate of Dang Gui Roast Duck, a plate of Shi Quan Roast Duck and a plate of Char Siew Roast Pork . The sauce of the Dang Gui Roast Duck was punched with full flavour. The sauce of the Shi Quan Roast Duck was diluted. The Char Siew and Roast Pork were pretty good. They offer many other cooked dishes too but I did not order. I was there for the roast duck.The duck was very tender and not gamey at all. It tastes very fresh to me. There is very little fat so there was no wastage. I could eat the entire duck me from the bones.Whole duck RM64Half duck RM33Quarter duck (thigh and drumstick area) RM19The elderly service staff was polite , attentive and responsive. Cash payment only. There is a money changer diagonally opposite the restaurant.The setting was old school, rustic but clean.With such affordable prices converted to SG Dollars and such good quality meat, I recommend Ya Wang !

Author: Chenyze LoveFood
Review: Pretty good roast meats place that also does some zichar dishes. The herbal roast duck (ginseng, ten herbs, Angelica root/tangkwei) are their specialty and so is the char siew. We went with the Ten Herbs option and the herbal aspect was …MorePretty good roast meats place that also does some zichar dishes. The herbal roast duck (ginseng, ten herbs, Angelica root/tangkwei) are their specialty and so is the char siew. We went with the Ten Herbs option and the herbal aspect was aromatic without being overly medicinal. The char siew was sticky and caramelised, but because it can be quite fatty you're better off with a smaller portion, I reckon. They do sell individuals portion of the meats too so it's good for single diners. Sweet potato leaves cooked sambal style were another standout dish, because of the smoky intensity of the sambal. That said, the sambal is so punchy in flavour that perhaps rice would work better than noodles. The dumpling soup is rather forgettable because the soup was bland save for the peppery accent; the dumplings were so chock-full of meat they reminded me of siew mai, but again the seasoning felt a bit muted. Service is pretty patient and friendly, though I was a bit taken aback when I returned the (chargeable) wet napkins and the waitress lady said they're charging it anyway, as tips for the staff. Didn't want to quibble because the amount is really quite little but I'd still felt a little unsettled.
Restaurant: Restoran Ya Wang 鸭皇药材烧腊大王

The duck meat around the boney parts was tough and chewy and the skin was half-crispy, half-soft but overall, it was quite lean with most of the fats underneath the skin all rendered off during roasting. What I really liked and which I thought was the hero of the dish was the subtly herbal sauce that was quite tasty. I was really surprised that they were the consultant for Dian Xiao Er because the herbal sauce at Dian Xiao Er was more robust and delicious than this. I had great roast ducks in Singapore before and while this was better in standard than the regular ones found in most hawker centres or coffee shops, it still wasn’t my type of roast duck. Author: HT Diong
Review: Location: The cafe is located in an industrial estate about 15 minutes drive from KSL. My friend and I took Grab there which costs about 11 rm (off-peak).Effciency: We arrived at about 11am. As it was a Sunday, we were expecting a big crowd there. Service is relatively fast for a big crowd, we waited about 30 minutes before our turn.Ambience: The interior of the cafe looks modern and chic while the staff are very attentive and friendly. Music was on the louder side, but still tolerable for both of us (the hard wall adds to the reverberation).Drink: They ran out of beans for filtered coffee, so I ordered a cup of Magic, a signature drink in Melbourne. I was looking forward to it as there are not many places in JB and Singapore that serve this. The milk texture is just right (I think the barista's skill is quite good), but the cup I had lacked the flavour and aroma, which I supposed it is due to where and how the coffee beans are sourced. If you are not picky, I would say the cup is decent, but it didn't have the wow factor for me.Food: My friends and I ordered Quesadilla Brekkie, which was the highlight of our trip there. Both of us like this dish and the creamy sauce is well balanced by the other components to this dish.  Overall, I feel this is a well concept dish and very well executed!We wished we hadn't ordered the roasted chicken thighs, which was disappointing and fell very much below our expectation. I personally wish the skin of the chicken could be more crispy. The meat is succulent, but both of us could taste that the meat is off. I would describe the taste as if the chicken thigh has been placed in room temperature for quite some time. Even the herbs on the chicken could not cover up the taste. When we flipped the thighs over we could see the cooked bone marrow oozing out on the lentil beans (which is a big no-no for me). We could not finish that dish unfortunately.Overall, I would think the cafe is decent and very much better as compared to other cafe in JB, but it didn't meet up to my anticipation and expectation. The quesadilla is good but the roasted chicken is way off the mark. Given the choice, I would hesitate to travel a long way on top of the 30 minutes waiting time (but I would probably give it a second chance because of the quesadilla).

Not even casual fine-dining. We sent back food by 2nd course.- was contemplating whether to just leave but we decided to see how the main course will turn out. Turns out we should have just leave the place, the main course is ridiculous!- Both food and experience FAIL. Seems like we’re dining in the dark.We’re plain unlucky, the only thing is that luckily we didn’t choose to stay at Hotel Jen because it ain’t worth it at all. 👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻 Even when we pass by the spa to get to skybar, the staff at the reception counter looked so unhappy to simply point and guide us the way to skybar.In the end, 1 pax dinner was waived out of goodwill. Author: Ruben Kumar M
Review: This joint was highly recommended by one of my friend in JB. So, I decided to drop by this corner lot restaurant somewhere near the JB City Square. It was about 7pm on a Friday, so there was plenty of space available. You can sit in the …MoreThis joint was highly recommended by one of my friend in JB. So, I decided to drop by this corner lot restaurant somewhere near the JB City Square. It was about 7pm on a Friday, so there was plenty of space available. You can sit in the indoor air-conditioned area or the outdoor open area here. The ambiance is really good, potrays the olden Western diner concept. It was not hot at all, the air-conditioning was excellent. Staff were quick, prompt and attentive. Service was excellent, the food came in no time (about 7 minutes after ordering). The chicken chop was perfectly fried, not too dry. But the small issue I had was there were small bones and I had to weed them out. The homemade mushroom sauce compliments well with the chicken. Coleslaw hits the spot as well, but the wedges was dry and hard. Probably need to improve on the wedges. The fried rice was decent, but the RM8 price tag is really expensive. The drinks as well can be cheaper. Pricing overall is a bit steeper, but the food quality was good enough to earn those price tags. Drinks probably not worth the price. Parking can be a challenge here.
Location: 17, Jalan Dhoby, Bandar Johor Bahru, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: isaac tan
Review: Tried the fried rice, fried chicken, grilled chicken, and ice cream jelly. Overall the meal started out great but got pretty weak over time. …MoreTried the fried rice, fried chicken, grilled chicken, and ice cream jelly. Overall the meal started out great but got pretty weak over time.The fried rice tastes great and I highly recommend it. The rice came out slightly hard, and maybe a little undercooked, but overall didnt impact the taste.The fried chicken has amazing crunchy texture, I would recommend trying it for that alone. The quality of the chicken and its overall flavour profile leaves much to be desired however. The first bite and experiencing the mouthwatering crunch and flavour affirms the expectation that the chicken is good, but the more you eat, the more you realise that the flavour itself is just on the batter, and the chicken itself is just bland and likely frozen chicken from the supermarket. With that said, you occasionally bite into some leftover bones not removed from the chicken, which makes no sense to me as you can't tell where the bones are with the batter overlaid on the chicken. Watch out for sharp bones when eating.The fried chicken itself could do with better seasoning to enhance the taste and make it more varied, the first bite is carried by the texture of the cooking, but falls off sharply afterward. Perhaps some pepper, cajun spice and/or basil could be added to give it some complexity as the saltiness is good enough.The grilled chicken can be summarised as a mushroom-sauce flavoured steak. Wouldn't recommend as the mushroom sauce tastes more like generic meat flavoured jelly than mushroom.The mushroom sauce to me is not worth spoiling your chicken or wedges over, wouldn't recommend using it. I havent tried the black pepper so you can potentially try that instead. I suggest asking for the sauce in a separate ramekin to try it at your own pace.The wedges themselves are soggy, but it appears that it is likely due to a different style of cooking, possibly a long soaking in salt water before a quick pan fry. If you like half cooked potato or mashed potatoes, its nice. Otherwise, don't come in expecting your normal deep fried wedges and order something else to go with your chicken instead.The ice cream jelly was an interesting dessert, I suggest trying that just for the uniqueness. The jelly is sinfully sweet, so watch out for that if you aren't a sweet tooth.

Author: Yvonne Tan
Review: Been here umpteen times since their opening when they had the ‘Chicken Up’ signboard. Both the young or old in our group love the food here. …MoreBeen here umpteen times since their opening when they had the ‘Chicken Up’ signboard. Both the young or old in our group love the food here.We had Spicy Yangnyeom wings at mild intensity and it’s very spicy to us (pick super spicy if you love the super spicy instant noodles challenge).Personally I prefer Honey Butter wings over Garlic Soya Wings. The price on their menu is also a good gauge for portion size for things such as fries and chicken wings (vs chicks).We had Bulgogi Fries which the kids love. We always order their melon bingsoo.Drinks wise, our hands-down favourite is lychee rita which is essentially a non-alcoholic slushie. We’ve had their mango and peach mojito ade before and it’s good too. During our latest visit, we ordered Nutella Madness and Kookies Madness. We find Nutella madness a bit weird as it has a strong nutty taste. Kookies madness is like caramel drink which is very sweet and lacking other taste. We’ll stick with their “cocktails” next time.K Fry is our must-visit food place whenever we are near KSL!There’s also a lift for pram users or elderly.

Author: Hilmi Hamdan
Review: Medan Selera Tepian Tebrau is often packed at night, and this speaks to how good the food and atmosphere is. I have been here twice so far and both times I went home wholly satisfied and with tapau (take aways) after a splendid dinner. …MoreMedan Selera Tepian Tebrau is often packed at night, and this speaks to how good the food and atmosphere is. I have been here twice so far and both times I went home wholly satisfied and with tapau (take aways) after a splendid dinner.Most of the stalls are packed even though the menus are varied, and as if mirroring this, Tepian Tebrau plays host to a variety of guests. The intense competition between the stalls fuels their passion to create amazing, even uniquely good food.On both my visits, I enjoyed the hospitality of Al Mizan, which serves Satay, Fried Rice, Fried Noodles,and their specialty here, Seafood. The Nasi Goreng Kambing was especially good, and amazingly void of any smell of goat, making it a must have for mutton lovers.Also, do sample their satay, which I found to be sweet yet intensely flavorful. The peanut sauce that they serve along with it provides the perfect accompaniment for their satay, sweet and flavorful, not delicate as often found at elsewhere.I saved the best for last, the seafood. I am not really a seafood lover, but I found the seafood here to be a real delight. We tried Siakap Bakar and Udang masak Kam Heong. We rarely have these dishes and wanted to try something new, fortunately, we were rewarded handsomely. Though the siakap was grilled, the chef managed to maintain the juiciness of the fished. Crowned with a generous topping of sambal pais, every spoonful was a burst flavors and subtle textures. The first three bites all I could say was 'wow, wow, wow', as I grappled for words in my attempt to expressed the emotions that boiled up. The udang Kam Heong did not disappoint either and proudly showcased the same intensity of flavor as the other dishes. As with the siakap, the first bite was shocking, albeit in a positive, uplifting way. My spirits we definitely lifted with that dish, and for brief moments I was blissfully oblivious to everything else around me.Though I have only tried one stall at Tepian Tebrau, I do recommend this place if you wish to experience lively food in a lively atmosphere. It'll make a great start to an evening where anything can happen.
Location: A31-06 paragon Residence, Straits View, Johor Bahru, Johor

So I told the staff in the restaurant that I would like for the steak to be on the grill slightly longer and they gladly took it back to the kitchen. When they come back, they gave me a new one which is something that I didn't expect them to do at all. This time they got it just right for me and I am really happy with how delicious the steak taste. Look at the photos and you will know what I am talking about.My colleague has a beer battered fish and chips that tasted really good as well. I think if I happened to return there for lunch or dinner again I'd definitely give this one a try.Also, our client is happy with his red snapper too!In overall, we had a great time there. Food and service are fantastic. Price is reasonable.Highly recommended!

Yes I do understand we have to give opportunities  for new staff to learn and pick up but the rest of the experienced crew who weren't busy engaging with diners  during then should also ensure that she carried out her duties rightfully eg. Making sure that she has passed the message to diners that dinner will only be served at 7pm especially when we came in at an awkwardly 1 hour earlier before dinner . There was also no mention in the dinner menu is from 7pm instead it was shown open daily .  Overall the staff did sound very apologetic for the mishap . My purpose of writing this feedback is just some tips that the management should look into how to further enhance their customer service so as to avoid such unhappiness . Author: Victor Tung Keat Chai
Review: (Translated by Google) The Johor Bahru, which entered the old street of Chen Xunian, seems to have entered the time tunnel -- the old time that disappeared. On the way of memories, the time gradually became slow. …More(Translated by Google) The Johor Bahru, which entered the old street of Chen Xunian, seems to have entered the time tunnel -- the old time that disappeared. On the way of memories, the time gradually became slow.The sunset slanted in the red mottled brick wall.I started to imagine black and white photos.In 1862, the old streets of Johor Bahru looked like a bustle.Remember which day of the year,Very long and short years,I can't see it, I can't go anywhere.Now I can't go back, the scene that has already passed away.Looking back, it has been for many years.Looking at the sky through the window,I am going back to this old street again.Listening to the dribbles of the time.#这的岁 seems to have an endless story#文青打卡必到地地(Original)踏进陳旭年老街的新山红馆，仿佛走入了时光隧道 -- 消失的舊時光，在回憶的路上，時間逐渐變得好慢。夕陽斜斜映在那玫红斑駁的磚牆，我對著黑白照片開始想像，一八六二年新山老街那熙来攘往的模样。记不得哪年的哪一天，很漫长又很短暂的岁月，看也看不到，去也去不了的地方。现在已经回不去，早已流逝的光景。回头望一眼，已经很多年的时间。透过窗缝间看着天，我再次回到这老街，听着那时光滴滴答答地流转。#这边的岁月仿佛有诉说不尽的故事#文青打卡必到之地

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Unbeknownst to all of you, I have a very good friend whom I am proud to call my brother in the southern state of Johor. We went to the same college, studied in the same foundation program before he went his separate way to Wellington while …MoreUnbeknownst to all of you, I have a very good friend whom I am proud to call my brother in the southern state of Johor. We went to the same college, studied in the same foundation program before he went his separate way to Wellington while I on the other hand, headed to Dunedin in New Zealand.We still keep in touch even after we graduated - he went back to his hometown in JB to kick-start his career and worked his way up the industry. He is now certified auditor with his own firm. No matter how busy he is, he will try to make some time to entertain me whenever I'm in town, as long as he's around. So this restaurant is a family friend of his, and now he's handling their accounts.We just blindly followed him into the restaurant and he ordered some of the dishes for us, with a bottle of Cordon Bleu to keep us entertained while waiting.◾Steamed fish - embarrassed to say this but I'd forgotten the type of fish but what I remember was that the fish was very fresh and steamed to perfection.◾Deep fried chicken leg - by far my favourite dish of the night. The chicken leg was actually braised first before deep fried, resulting in the explosion of flavours inside the mouth. I think that we had 2 servings that evening◾Stir fried asparagus with prawns - sweet asparagus plus sweet prawns.. great combinations.◾Fried kuey teow - this wasn't planned.. but we were already quite high high by then (Cordon Bleu) and one of us said "I'm still feeling hungry" so my friend quickly ordered this char kuey teow. I must say that the CKT was very good - packed with the essential wok hei, the cockles were cooked just right... For someone who try to avoid eating carb, u found myself breaking the rules again.. sigh!!This is a well established restaurant that has been in business for many many years. The service was attentive - maybe because my friend was around - and we ended the night happily.
Location: 1-5, Jalan Keris, Taman Sri Tebrau, Johor Bahru, Johor

Dish was almost tasteless!2) Cockles - We ordered 500g (lucky us!) and ended up eating less than 10 pieces of it. We told the lady at the counter and fortunately she did not charge us for it.3) Capcai - Only vege inside. No other protein in it. Be warned. I know its a mixed vege dish but what I've had at other stall comes with snall prawn and squid.4) The only seafood that's fresh as i chose the most alive looking. But sadly the dish was ruined by the black pepper sauce. Tasted like bottled black pepper sauce drowned the crab.Overall, it was a bad experience for me. It was my first time there after a friend's recommendation. Food was horrible and service was even worst. Most of the staff were busy sitting down chit chatting than serving customers. Definitely be my last visit there and will definitely not recommend anyone going there. Don't waste your time.

Review: What a surprising find for a restaurant! Just right above the famous Lavender bakery, you will discover this beautifully set up restaurant. The setting of the diner was so appropriate for Christmas, Christmas decorations everywhere with …MoreWhat a surprising find for a restaurant! Just right above the famous Lavender bakery, you will discover this beautifully set up restaurant. The setting of the diner was so appropriate for Christmas, Christmas decorations everywhere with just the right amount of subtlety.The accompanying music piped in was just perfect.Now, for the food; we couldn't ask for more. Other than the slightly colder squid ink pasta, the food was exquisite. The seafood was fresh and lightly seasoned. The pasta was not soggy, but at the right texture for us. We found the cold pasta with prawns a perfect start for dinner. If I need to find a needle in the haystack, just to complain, the ingredients could be a little more generous. We wanted to try the apple pie and unfortunately for us, it was sold out. What a shame! It must be one of the celebrated desserts in the restaurant.The waiting staff was attentive and fast. They provided the right amount of information on the food and informed us about a ”Live” Band playing in the restaurant on Wednesday and Friday. The crew were terrific.If you want a fun and enjoyable evening, you wouldn't be disappointed in this restaurant.

If you’re craving for Asam Fish, go check out Dulang Lima Cafe or Restaurant Nyonya Treats Cuisine at Taman Perling with more variety of palatable dishes with spices. Each of the set consisted another 2 fried dish of our choices (chicken, catfish etc), supplemented with ulam (salads), flavoured sauce of our choices (belacan, budu, cincalok) and 2 of rice. Each dulang costed us RM25 (for 2 pax).We added fried Tempe and scrambled eggs and altogether with 4 drinks we were charged about RM94. We were not disappointed as the taste was above our expectation and beyond our satisfaction and it was so delicious it worth every cents we spent.The service was pretty quick as opposed to majority of the reviews here saying it was too slow. Maybe luck was on our side.We paid using Maybank QR Pay and it was hassle free. Did I tell you the premise was spotless clean? Yes it was, impressively! The parking area was ample (at least during our experience that time).We will definitely be back soon enough.Thank you. It is highly recommended for authentic traditional Malay cuisine lover.

Author: Ivan Ling
Review: We went for the hot pot instead of the barbecue, which was confusing, because when I searched for Chigui Hotpot, it doesn't show on Google maps. It was only when I reached the venue, that I realized Tanba and Chigui was connected, …MoreWe went for the hot pot instead of the barbecue, which was confusing, because when I searched for Chigui Hotpot, it doesn't show on Google maps. It was only when I reached the venue, that I realized Tanba and Chigui was connected, nonetheless, the interior was awesome.In terms of food, the meat was great. Go for the prawn paste if you are going for their hotpot. The prawn paste is served to the table as a bowl of raw paste, which you will then cook by the spoonfuls in the hotpot. It was really quite an experience.The ambiance was great, and I was puzzled because the whole place doesn't smell like a hotpot restaurant (usually these places are hot, and filled with smokes), I guess the high ceiling and good ventilation helps. The hotpots were cooked in the traditional way, using charcoals. So you might want to be careful when the workers are changing the charcoals. Trust me, you don't want those hot charcoals to fall on you.They have a great selection of sauce to go with your hotpot, but do mind that they charge RM3 per pax for the sauce (if you want to help your self to their awesome selection).All and all, it was a great experience, I was there to celebrate a friend's birthday, and our table is around 8 pax. We got 4 types of soup filled in 2 pots (yinyang pots fill 2 types of soups each). The total damage was about RM80 per pax.

I prefer fresh meat with little seasoning but marinated to perfection and then smoked for 4-5hrs so didn't really like the BBQ taste which covers the natural flavors of the meat. Brisket and pulled lamb was good although the lamb had a strong meat smell. You can't change the sides when ordering the preset menu(wanted to change coleslaw to onion rings). I wouldn't go here for a second time going for the expensive menu... The ala carte with sides to choose from is good enough I guess. Recommended to try but it's cheaper to go for the 100g menu to get a taste of it first. Overall just felt that it wasn't up to standard for the premium prices charged.

Not quite the Klang herbal version, but more similar to the SG version without the pepper. While the Bak kut teh is a must try, the seasame oil chicken is to die for.Starting with the BKT. The soup stock is good, slightly herbal and a bit more sweet then savory, though subtle. Nice pieces of chopped up pork ribs, although i feel the meat could have been boiled longer to be more tender. It's also came with pork liver and extra orders of bean curd skin, golden & butter mushroom. The butter mushroom though i could have done without.As for the sesame oil chicken it is The Dish, served bubbling hot in a claypot (if only i could have uploaded the video). Cooked in a black sesame oil based sauce with ginger, it is full of flavor and goes well with a bowl of rice.Next time i will also try the white wine chicken claypot.It's located at an open air corner coffee shop with ample parking along the road.
Restaurant: Restaurant Shun Fa Bak Kut Teh

Author: lovelynettetan
Review: Back with the entire family for a glorious feast this time!8-9 dishes averaging 1 dish per pax (that's actually quite a good gauge,  6 …MoreBack with the entire family for a glorious feast this time!8-9 dishes averaging 1 dish per pax (that's actually quite a good gauge,  6 dishes for 6 pax, 4 dishes for 4 pax etc)Started off with their signature pancake bee hoon and sambal chilli - 2 big plates for 9 paxThen it was 5-spice meat roll that really packed a punch of wholesome goodness.The fish slices cooked in Malaysia's unique "kam heong" or golden fragrance stir fry style was a sure winner with an ideal mix of aromatic curry leaves and powder, dried shrimp, and savory bean paste.Next,  we had prawn paste chicken, a dish we spotted almost on every other table in the restaurant that night.Deep fried pork was yet another star dish. Fried to a golden crisp, the sizzling hot oil did little to diminish its full flavour and tasty marinade.The "petai" and sambal anchovies with a generous splatter of onions was yet another familiar family favourite.Salted fish and stewed pork belly served in clay pot was a pleasantly heartwarming dish. My dad spotted it on their signature signboard - good ol' number 13. We ordered the smallest portion just to try but it left such an indelible impression and great aftertaste.To be honest,  the steam fish with a generous sprinkling of preserved radish or "chai poh" was nothing to shout about but the freshness of the fish more than made up for it.I must say that the signature tofu was a hit with both adults and children. Crispy on the outside, creamy in the inside - a must try.Rounding up the evening with traditional yam paste was a dream. Gingko nuts, steamed pumpkin, and fragrant onion oil all mixed in with fluffy, yummy yam paste completed the whole dining experience.The final bill came up to less than RM300.We'll definitely be back for seconds!
Location: 38, Jalan Sultanah Aminah, Taman Iskandar, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: Amirul Asyrofudin
Review: Mat Corner at Medan Selara Mahsuri in Bandar Baru Uda is one of the best known nasi ambang stalls in Johor Bahru. …MoreMat Corner at Medan Selara Mahsuri in Bandar Baru Uda is one of the best known nasi ambang stalls in Johor Bahru.Mat Corner is popular with local residents, workers and students in the Bandar Baru Uda (BBU) area.Mat Corner founded by Haji Mat in 2000 is synonymous with nasi ambang in Johor Bahru. The stall is now run by Haji Mat's three sons, Alwi, Udin and Pen.Mat Corner's food such as their crispy fried chicken is freshly cooked at the stall.Each plate of nasi ambang is given a splash of Mat Corner's signature sambal chili.The fiery looking sambal chili smothering the rice certainly looks intimidating, but it is just right for me. The sambal chili is spicy, savoury and sweet with spice flavours and aroma.Mat Corner uses good quality long grain rice for their nasi ambang.The freshly fried chicken is crispy golden brown outside and juicy tender inside. The chicken is infused with mild spices so it is flavoursome with hints of spicy heat.The "special" version (RM7) comes with beef rendang (in addition to the standard fried chicken). The tender beef rendang cubes are tender and juicy. Every bite releases the perfume of spices infused in it's fibres.There were a couple of these tiny, not too salty crispy salted fish on the plate.The look of this golden brown tempeh (soy bean cakes) makes me hungry.A small clump of savoury sweet serunding kelapa (fried spiced grated coconut ) completes the dish.Mat Corner's nasi ambang is one of Johor Bahru's most popular. Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Wow! Just wow... I had totally forgotten about this wonderful place until a dear friend of mine brought me here recently. I had come here about 10 years ago, had a great lunch with my customer and vowed to come back here again. A decade has …MoreWow! Just wow... I had totally forgotten about this wonderful place until a dear friend of mine brought me here recently. I had come here about 10 years ago, had a great lunch with my customer and vowed to come back here again. A decade has passed and if not for my friend, I'd never rediscover this restaurant.As the name suggest, the specialty is fish.. but oddly it was not steam fish but fried fish that took the centerstage. We will get to that later. Located in between Taman Sentosa and Taman Pelangi, coming here during peak hours and you might have to wait for table. Spacious and airy, you won't feel stuffy or hot.◾Fried fish - using red snapper, they de-boned and cut the fish in their own way before coated in light batter and deep fried. If not for the tail of the fish, you would not be able to tell what it is. Just cut off the chunks of meat and savour the fresh, sweet and tender fish which was sweet and savoury as they use combination of Thai sweet chilly sauce, dark soy sauce, mayonnaise and spring onion. Marvellous!◾Stir fried shark lip - do look out for available fresh seafood in the chiller. My friend spotted the last plate of this collagen goodness stuff and proceed to order it. They stir fried it and served.. I walloped most of it.◾Stuffed ma yao fish - the tedious process of de-boning the fish, minced the meat and then stuffed back the meat before deep fried. Love it but still overshadowed by the fried fish.◾Dong po yuk - served in their own sauce which was not too thick (like those we get in Klang Valley) together with beancurd skin, it didn't feel too heavy to go with our meal.As a testament on how good the fish is, you will see at least a plate of fried fish (just say 炸鱼) on each and every table.
Location: 120, 100, Jalan Keris, Taman Sri Tebrau, Johor Bahru, Johor

Review: Out of the normWhen I was in JB, my friend would always bring me to his usual eateries as he …MoreOut of the normWhen I was in JB, my friend would always bring me to his usual eateries as he was a creature of habits - but for me, I would love to try other options since I seldom go down South now. Therefore on my last trip, I scoured through my list to see which one I had not been to.. and then I demanded to go there.Sze Zai Hiong is located few doors down the road from my favourite watering hole, JJ Wine & Tapas in Taman Pelangi. This restaurant has basic restaurant setup but with air-conditioned, something which I appreciate especially when having lunch under hot weather.◾claypot mixed vegetables with tong fun - something not so heavy-flavoured for the rather heavy lunch.◾stir fried lady fingers with salted egg yolk - crunchy texture covered with savoury salted egg yolk.◾ham yue fa lam bou aka claypot pork belly with salted fish - I prefer stronger taste for this dish and it didn't disappoint. In fact, it was so good with my bowl of rice.◾stir fried lala with pork lard - THE REASON I came here.. the sight of fresh clams and pork lards together was a case of foodgasm. The cili padi lent the dish some spicy kick. I enjoyed it... A must order for first timer◾steamed shark meat (limited availability) with superior soy sauce and minced ginger - full of collagen goodness, and I must say that the flavour hit the right spot for me.◾Chinese steamed egg topped generously with fried garlic and spring onions - gotta love it when they were generous with fried garlic and spring onions.I almost had food coma after finishing everything - as there were only three of us but the sacrifice was so worth it. I drove back to KL with a happy tummy.
Location: 62, Jalan Pingai, Taman Pelangi, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: Ayla Tan
Review: Love love love love love the "French beans with Pu Er Leaves". Such a unique dish and it tastes good; the fresh beans are crisp with a tinge of sweetness from the tea leaves. Would definitely go back for this dish again. …MoreLove love love love love the "French beans with Pu Er Leaves". Such a unique dish and it tastes good; the fresh beans are crisp with a tinge of sweetness from the tea leaves. Would definitely go back for this dish again.The served appetiser (you do need to pay for them) is the beans and guava. We rejected the beans because we don't take them but I enjoyed the guava though the ones in Thailand are definitely better.The vegetable dishes were generally yummy. We ordered the Brinjal and the Fried Yam, both of which tasted good.The noodle soup is also delicious because the soup is rich and the noodle's texture is just right. Same goes for our lotus peanut pork rib soup which also tastes yummy, though I'm pretty sure my mum, who's a very good cook, can also do the same.The only dish that we didn't enjoy is the drunken chicken - we didn't enjoy the flavour of the seasoning/marination as we find the taste of the wine overpowering. Oh yes, the sour plum drink wasn't to my liking as well but the rest of my companions enjoyed it. Should try the honey green tea the next time round.Though I've read reviews of the bad service, we personally enjoyed quite good service there. The lady who introduced the dishes to four of us advised us about the right quantity of food for the four of us, which really did turn out to be very accurate. Dishes were served promptly and the staff is sufficiently attentive. Would definitely be back again.
Location: J4-21, City Square, 106-108, Jalan Wong Ah Fook, Bandar Johor Bahru, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: Dolorosa Lin
Review: It was around Sept-Nov 2018. A Chinese grab driver told us to try JB's specialty kway teow kia. As a non Chinese speaker (and reader) we got soooooooo confused when he showed us (many times) those Chinese characters saying "kway teow kia" …MoreIt was around Sept-Nov 2018. A Chinese grab driver told us to try JB's specialty kway teow kia. As a non Chinese speaker (and reader) we got soooooooo confused when he showed us (many times) those Chinese characters saying "kway teow kia" each time we passed thtough the restos. tried to remember them but.. nope..nothing inside my head.So we asked our next driver and got confused together because apparently this guy didn't know much abt the dish. Too sad.Then we tried to google with a very minimum infos..and I didn't even know how to spell it. But somehow found something. So we drove to where the gps took us and...nothing there.Sooo..we decided to take our walk from around Jl. Abiat..at 9/10 p.m., some 30 minutes walk..and we saw Hi Wan. Still not sure if that's the place.Moved closer and saw something noodle-like..so we asked the staff. With tooooo big languange barrier (they speak Chinese, we speak English)...finally decided to order 2 portions.Sooo glad that it's the one we're looking for!!!Clean but tasty broth, flat noodle made of (i think) rice flour, TASTY chili sauce!!!!!!! I had no idea what toppings I took, but one of em which looks like some meats wrapped in tofu skin TASTED HEAVENLY!!!!!!Surprisingly!!! We spent only MYR 15-17 for them..and 2 drinks. Which means @MYR 2 for kway teow, @MYR 1.5 for liang tea, and some MYR 8 for 2 toppings.ARGGHHHHH...I NEED TO MOVE TO JB A.S.A.P. and spend my pennies for Hi Wan for the rest of my life!!!PLEASE...DO...TRY...HI WAN! ❤️
Location: 210, Jalan Sri Pelangi, Taman Pelangi, Johor Bahru, Johor

Author: N.a.d S
Review: Been here a couple of times and love the food. So I'm just going to do a review for lunch and dinner (we went on different occasions) at one go. …MoreBeen here a couple of times and love the food. So I'm just going to do a review for lunch and dinner (we went on different occasions) at one go.Ambience:The place is well decorated interior-wise. The artificial Sakura tree does give a Japanese theme to it. Restrooms are clean and so is everywhere else in the restaurant. The staff was always going around cleaning, that's a great point.Dinner:We were recommended to take the special yakiniku platter which consists of 8 types of cut. The waiter was kind enough to demo and cook for us and he said during busy hours, they could just do the demo.- Yakiniku 8 types: Great! Value for money as well. My favourite cut is the Sotomomo. The meat is super tender and it just melted in my mouth. The platter is specially marinated in a few types of fruit which gives a sour taste but with sprinkles of black pepper and salt, the taste isn't distinctive. A special dip was served together with the meat but it wasn't for me as it had strong taucu taste but it is supposed to go well with the meat. We like our meat medium rare so basically just 30-45 secs for each side depending on the cut.- Chicken Teriyaki: Taste different from a typical Malaysionised Japanese restaurant. The batter coat was really thin, which is good because you don't get quesy easily. The amount of teriyaki sauce coat is also minimal retaining the taste of the chicken. Definitely for future order.- Scallop on grill: Don't remember what it's called but it was part of the monthly promotion. It didn't taste anything special, my partner loved it tho, but if I were to compare, I love meat on the grill better. Good for seafood enthusiast.Lunch:- We ordered our favorite Yakiniku Platter. Taste great but this time around, the cuts were more marble, it was juicier and more tender. This is our all time favourite. Actually this set is alot for 2 pax, could also be shared by 3-4. Towards the end of the meal, we almost couldn't finish our food, but to avoid wastage, we forced ourself 😂- Hotate Mentai for appetizer. The amount of cheese/cream was right and it was flamed torched giving it a slightly burnt taste. I prefer this over the grilled scallop but my partner preferred the grilled scallop. Personal preference.- Lunch Set of Teriyaki Chicken. The teriyaki chicken was different compared to the dinner but portion was just as big. The chicken was a bit crispy on the top, I preferred the former version. The chicken was on a bed of rice with salad and eggs. Came with side dishes of  miso, cawanmushi, gyozas, and pickles. Gyoza was a bit overcooked but it did not spoil the overall experience.- There was a few selection of lunch set and I must say that the lunches are value for money. Our next visit might also be during lunch as I find it more relaxing compared to dinner (even tho the window is short). We really took our time to enjoy the food compared to dinner where we were in a rush because it was almost closing hour.Anything else?- Love the sauce/dip bar. The condiments are readily available for guests to try each and one of it. My favourite would be the spicy soy sauce and the green sambal. It's really spicy 🔥 so not for the faint of heart. There are other  sauce options.- Free flow of green tea. You can get it yourself or the staff as they refill everytime they see the glass is empty.- The staffs were really sweet and attentive BUT during lunch I was a bit annoyed. Nothing big but I feel like it needs to be mentioned here for constructive criticism -- we drove a normal car, nothing fancy and when we wanted to park at the designated parking area for customers, a slim chinese waitress was running towards us to let us know that we can't park there. I asked her if the place is closed, she said no and without apologizing -- let us in 🤔 We are plain simple folks but we do enjoy a good meal 😊 so please don't judge. Customer service should go on par with the food. For this, it lose a star in the review.
Location: 25c, Jalan Dato Abdullah Tahir, Taman Abad, Johor Bahru, Johor

The “siu” is “less” in Cantonese.11) Kopi-gah-dai = Coffee with extra sugar. The “gah” is “more” in Cantonese.
